name: Self-monitored blood pressure — home readings
description: A woman recording her own blood pressure at home, or a health worker entering the series she brings in. Each reading is a systolic/diastolic pair with the first-of-session flag the averaging protocol needs, plus the danger-sign question that routes straight to urgent care.
sourceGuideline: WHO SMART SMBP DAK v1.0.0; WHO recommendations on antenatal care (2016)

definition.title: Self-monitored blood pressure — home readings
definition.description: Readings plus the danger-sign question. Each reading routes to the SHR; the series is reduced to an escalation by the clinical-knowledge platform, not stored as a verdict on this form.

sections.title: A blood-pressure reading
sections.description: One pair per reading. Where readings come from a connected home device they are held by the monitoring service and need not be re-entered here; this form is the manual path.

fields.label: First reading of this sitting
fields.description: The first reading of a sitting is discarded from the average as a rest artefact — but never from the severe check. Marking it lets the average be computed the way the protocol intends.

options.display: No — a repeat in the same sitting

sections.title: Any danger signs today?
sections.description: Asked with every submission. A danger sign routes straight to urgent care whatever the readings say.

fields.label: Any of: severe headache, blurred vision, severe upper-abdominal pain, breathing difficulty, vaginal bleeding, convulsions, fever, severe vomiting
fields.description: The SMBP danger-sign list. Present routes to 'go right away' independent of the blood pressure. Blank is not 'no' — leave it unanswered rather than guessing.
